See module docstring's VALIDATION for why this parameter, checked directly rather than assumed. Also returns the labeled blur-island array and its label count, so `_element_groupings` can cross-reference Group A's own elements against the same blur pass without redoing it.

deterministic/segmentation.py.doc: Tier 1 deterministic element/residue segmentation, computed directly from a painting's TIFF master at native 16-bit precision -- no model call. Replaces Step 1 of `master_evidence_prompt.md`'s current job of having the model visually find every distinct ink deposit and tag it by eye: this module finds every ink deposit via connected-component analysis on a thresholded ink mask, splits any mass containing more than one distinct gestural direction (see ORIENTATION_* constants below), and assigns tags by real computed size, not a human's estimate of size order.

defs._blob_cells: Cells this blob's actual mask (not just its bounding box) occupies above MIN_CELL_OVERLAP_PIXELS. Always returns at least one cell (the single best-overlapping one) even if none clear that threshold -- checked directly against real T_119 data: at MIN_CELL_OVERLAP_PIXELS=20, 58% of genuine small residue marks (drips, splatter) overlap no cell enough to register at all, which would make every one of them an unlocatable blob rather than a small mark that's still somewhere specific on the sheet. A blob is only truly cell-less if its mask is empty, which shouldn't reach this function at all (NOISE_FLOOR_PIXELS is filtered before here).
defs._contour_for: Simplified boundary polygon in global pixel coords, from a mask already cropped to `bbox` (min_row, min_col, max_row, max_col) -- see _blob_cells' docstring for why local, not full-canvas.
defs._orientation_field: Structure-tensor local orientation (radians, from the vertical axis, matching skimage's own convention -- see Blob.orientation_deg) and coherence (0..1, how confidently a single direction dominates at that pixel) at the given window size.
defs._find_angle_peaks: Real local maxima of a weighted circular histogram of doubled angles (mod 2*pi), smoothed, kept only if their PROMINENCE (height above their own surrounding valley, not absolute height -- see this module's SHIPPED/KNOWN LIMITATION comment above for why prominence, not height) clears PEAK_MIN_PROMINENCE_FRACTION of the total weight. Returns peak centers in the same doubled-angle space. Empty if there's no confident data at all.
defs._circular_distance: Distance from each angle in `a` to `peak`, both mod 2*pi, on the circle (never more than pi).
defs._nearest_peak: Index of the nearest peak per pixel; same result as argmin over the stacked distances (first index wins a tie) without holding one full-size distance array per peak.
defs._split_by_orientation: Split one connected ink blob into sub-masks by dominant local direction, per this module's ORIENTATION_*/HISTOGRAM_*/PEAK_* constants (see the block comment above them for why this shape of algorithm, and what was tried and rejected first). `mask` is a boolean array local to the blob's own bounding box (not the full image). Returns a list of boolean sub-masks covering `mask`'s True pixels between them -- a single-entry list if the blob has only one dominant direction, i.e. this is a safe no-op for an ordinary single-gesture element.
defs._frozen_region: The seven region properties this module reads, evaluated now. A regionprops region from a full-canvas label image keeps that image (int64, ~150 MB here) alive for as long as the region lives; with 10+ orientation-split sub-blobs that was the 2026-09-23 memory-cap failure on T_135/T_136/T_138 (+0.17 GB per kept sub-blob).
defs._blob_element_distances: {id(region): {element tag: min distance from any of the blob's pixels to that element}}, tags in element order. Both attachment passes need only these per-blob minima, so each element's full-canvas distance field is built, read and dropped one at a time. Holding one float64 field per element at once was the 2026-09-23 memory-cap failure on multi-element and 25 MP+ sheets (T_215, T_302, T_324, T_326, T_327: six fields alone took T_302 from 1.8 to 3.0 GB).
defs._attach_by_proximity: Per-BLOB attachment pass: a small blob within `threshold_px` (mask-to-mask, not centroid-to-centroid -- centroid distance is misleading against a long stroke) of a real element is that element's splatter -- see the ATTACHMENT_* block comment above for why this exists (T_119's 1108-blob mega-population). Blobs with no element nearby fall through to `isolated`, which is only ever clustered among ITSELF (see `_cluster_small_blobs`) -- never every small blob in the painting at once, which would let dense splatter near one element transitively drag in blobs from anywhere else on the canvas (real bug, found 2026-09-17 by testing exactly that: a single first-pass attempt at clustering-before-attachment collapsed T_219's entire 3405-blob residue field into one cluster).
defs._cluster_small_blobs: Cluster a set of small blobs into spatial groups by real pixel distance between centroids, deliberately NOT by the 6x3/3x6 cell grid. That grid exists only so a human/model can name a location in the schema's own vocabulary ("B2"); it has nothing to do with how far apart two marks actually are, and using it for a clustering decision was a real bug: with only 18 cells total, transitive cell-adjacency chains almost any two blobs together eventually (checked directly on T_119: all 1108 candidate blobs merged into one "population" spanning nearly the whole sheet). Cells are computed per blob only for the final report (via `_blob_cells`, already scale-appropriate for that purpose), never for this decision.
defs._reattach_clusters: Second attachment pass, at CLUSTER granularity -- real bug fixed 2026-09-17, found by Pete's direct visual check against T_219: three of its four residue populations (P2, P3, P4) were, by his own read of the actual painting, real splatter trailing from M1 or M2, not independent events. `_attach_by_proximity`'s tight per-blob threshold had already caught each cluster's nearest members as splatter in the first pass; what was left in each cluster missed that tight threshold individually even though the group as a whole is still plainly trailing from the same element -- a physically continuous trail shouldn't be split down the middle by where a per-blob cutoff happens to fall.
defs._finalize_residue: Turn already-formed clusters that survived both attachment passes independent (see `_cluster_small_blobs` / `_reattach_clusters`) into the final individual-vs-population report. A small cluster (at or below POPULATION_MIN_COUNT) is reported as individually-tagged blobs; a larger one is collapsed into one PopulationSummary.

CONCEPT.one_line: VAE V22 looks at a photographed sumi-ink painting the way a trained critic would, but with measurement doing everything measurement can: Python measures the sheet, a model judges only what cannot be measured, independent model readings are voted (two, plus a third only to break a split), and code turns the settled judgments into a 1-10 rating.
CONCEPT.audience_note: this spec serves two uses: explaining the VAE to others (read concept_model first) and operating/maintaining it (everything after)
problem: Peter Yuill paints large abstract sumi-ink works (mega-brushes, Chinese papers, ~97x180 cm), a year-long Crucible Year practice of 368+ numbered works T_001..
he wants an accurate, trackable 1-10 rating per work, comparable across the year, to see what improved and how

previous engines (V7/V10/V10C) felt 'only slightly better than a guess'; they rewarded heavy, textured, layered material load, which is Peter's baseline, not his quality: T_323 (Peter 5) scored 9 and T_326 (Peter 6) scored 10
a first V22 attempt decomposed judgment into a 14-step, per-cell evidence cascade; two blind reads of the same paintings disagreed on 30-70% of axes, so finer decomposition did not buy reliability
approach: measure first: deterministic Python on the 16-bit TIFF master measures every property that can be measured (ink masses, edges, overlaps, stroke paths, weight, unpainted voids, stroke orientation, edge contact, presence) and hands those to the model as facts that outrank its own reading
judge lean: the model answers one categorical question per axis, choosing a rung on a fixed five-rung ladder, writing its observation before its choice and naming what fails the next rung up
buy consistency by ensembling: the same lean call is run three times independently and voted; disagreement is reported as unresolved, never averaged

make rarity structural: the top rung ('master') means the excellent quality held everywhere without exception plus one further property, proven by a complete survey, and it only survives if every run independently awards it with high confidence; Python checks the survey against the measurements
keep the number out of the model: the model never sees a score; code computes the rating from the settled rungs with weights Peter can read and change
how_it_works: Step 1 (Python, zero model calls): from the TIFF, find ink (darkest 5 of 9 tonal bands), split it into elements, splatter and residue; profile every edge (crisp, soft, broken, bloom-like); find cells where passes overlap and how many tonal bands they hold; trace each stroke's path, width and endpoints; count masses and weight displacement; find held voids (paper with ink on opposite sides) and how crisp their limits are; read the main and second stroke orientation families (axial, so they locate directions without saying which way a mark travelled); record where ink meets each sheet edge and where weight sits against the sheet's centre, centre lines and edge midpoints; measure presence (ink coverage, share of the sheet in the two darkest tones, deepest ink against paper, edge-kind mix)
Step 1 output is validated against Peter's eye via colour overlays, never against a model

Step 2 (model): one prompt per painting carries the measured facts in plain cell-named English plus five views of the sheet (the photograph, a greyscale with a red 6x3 grid, a hand-picked close-up crop, an inverted view showing unpainted paper as shape, a low-pass view showing weight); the model names the sheet's parts, then classifies 14 axes

Step 2 (code): validate each run's JSON under its schema version and check it agrees with itself (a self-contradicting axis loses only its vote), cap any rung-4 claim whose survey contradicts a measurement, vote the runs per axis (run 3 only as a tie-break on axes runs 1 and 2 split), apply the master gate, compute the rating with its coverage and bounds
Step 3 (model, later): turns the settled findings into readable critical prose in four sections plus a free response ('NEON'), forbidden to change any finding

axes_plain.A1: Material Control: did the ink's behaviour on this paper stay governed; rare = a material behaviour (a halted bleed, a contained bloom) doing structural work where loss was likeliest
axes_plain.A2: Edge Command: do edge kinds vary with structural role; rare = an edge alone carries a relationship (a crisp shared edge locks ink and void)
axes_plain.A3: Stroke Conviction: do principal strokes read as committed continuous acts; rare = a full-length stroke with the marks of speed on it that stays sound in every phase; NOT_PRESENT when no stroke can be judged as an act
axes_plain.B1: Layer Architecture: do overlapping passes stay distinct with consistent depth; rare = the darkest register confined to structural positions
axes_plain.B2: Resolution: did the sheet stop where its structure was complete (no clutter in voids, unresolved ends, filling, retrace); rare = every part costs something if removed
axes_plain.C1: Void: is unpainted paper a shaped, load-bearing part of the structure; rare = void and ink lock at shared junctions with findable limits (crisp or soft) and the void reads as a shape in its own right
axes_plain.C2: Equilibrium: how the weight is handled, displaced or centred; rare = balance held by opposing forces (two movements, or a movement and a void), not mass alone
axes_plain.C3: Directional Structure: what organises movement; rare = two opposing movements unified by a shared centre, void or axis, or one full-length movement every other part takes its direction from
axes_plain.C4: Frame Engagement: how the structure meets the four edges; rare = three or more edges each doing a different named job, or composed margins around a contained structure, with the structure placed against the sheet
axes_plain.C5: Load-Bearing Parts: do parts beyond the primary carry load nothing else could; rare = removing a part changes a property of the primary itself
axes_plain.D1: Chance Integration: what the painting did with chance events (bloom, splatter, drip); rare = the event is built into the structure by a named visible route and the passage's structure depends on it (judged on what the sheet shows, not how it came about)
axes_plain.D2: Visual Cadence: where a unit repeats, does the sequence do something; rare = a deliberate break in the sequence that the structure uses
axes_plain.D3: Risk: how difficult was what the sheet attempted, and did it hold; rare = two or more high-difficulty acts hold and the sheet's principal relation depends on both; on watch (Peter 2026-09-24): the calibration report tests whether it adds anything beyond A1/A3/C1/C3
axes_plain.E1: Presence: does the sheet register with force at viewing distance (added v2.1 after T_188); not coverage: one decisive dark stroke on open paper can command a sheet, pale blurred wash can barely register; rare = the darkest ink meets the brightest paper at a structural junction or void, so force and structure are one event

rung_meaning.0: structural failure (in a structural position, recurring, or dominating the sheet): occasional
rung_meaning.2: strong: a named quality clearly achieved: common
rung_meaning.3: excellent: the quality in a compound demanding form: occasional
rung_meaning.4: master: rung 3 held everywhere without exception plus a further property: rare

CONCEPT.rating: weighted mean rung (0-4) mapped through anchors 0->1, 1->5, 2->7, 3->9, 4->10, joined linearly, so the whole 1-10 scale is reachable (the ends are fixed; calibration moves the interior anchors); pre-calibration weights: E1 x3, structural C1-C4 x2, A2 A3 B2 C5 D1 x1, A1 B1 D2 D3 x0.5; unresolved applicable axes are reported as weight coverage plus a low/high rating range, and a result is provisional below 80% coverage or with a weight-2+ axis unsettled
what_failed_before: V21.5-derived ladders on a 10-painting run: floor rungs fired on single instances (PHASE_FAILURE 7/10, WORKED_PAST_REPEATEDLY 7/10), top rungs passed easily (5/10), some axes never discriminated (COHERENT 9/10), two axes never produced a value
the model's own read of how many ink masses a sheet has disagreed with itself on 4 of 10 paintings across sessions, whatever facts it was given: gestalt judgments are volatile, so V22 measures them
evidence_so_far: hand-check of six Peter-rated works against the new ladders (not a model run): the structural axes C1-C4 separate Peter's 9s (T_333, T_338, T_317) from his 5s and 6s (T_326, T_323, T_327) the way he did, while material/layer axes A1/B1 do not: layering is his baseline
what his 9s have and his 5s lack: a held, clean, load-bearing void; opposing movements unified; balance carried by direction; structure placed against the sheet's edges

Step 1 overlays checked on T_128, T_313, T_323, T_326, T_328: voids, movements and edge contact read correctly except large voids beyond ~40% of the short side (T_326's arc interior) which are not measured

first model runs (Opus 5.5, v2): T_316 engine 6.9 vs Peter 7 and T_328 7.9 vs Peter 9, both accepted final; runs 1 and 2 agreed on 10 of 13 axes each time (the archived granular prompt disagreed on 30-70%)

T_188 engine 7.3 vs Peter's blind 3-4: the first clear miss; the engine had no measure of whether a sheet registers at all, rule 7 let fragments carry axes, the bleed never met the rung-0 bar; v2.1 is the response

presence across the 20 rated measured works: darkest-tone share tracks Peter's rating best (Spearman 0.49), coverage barely (0.17), soft edges weakly against (-0.23); T_313 (Peter 9) is sparse (34% coverage), so presence is defined as force, not coverage
a Sonnet 5 check on T_316 was consistent (12 of 13 axes agree) at about 0.6 of the cost but leaned one rung high on six axes; Opus 5.5 stays the engine model

T_188 on v2.1 (two runs): 7.8 provisional; the runs agree with each other (11 of 14 axes) but award rungs for one qualifying local feature and never weigh how much of the sheet works; E1 went to ARRESTING on a single junction while the sheet's deepest ink (0.15) is the palest of 21 measured rated works. Conclusion (Peter): the ladders' qualifications are too lenient
accuracy is unproven until the 16-work calibration set is run and reported

pipeline.name: deterministic measurement
pipeline.input: TIFF 16-bit master /mnt/c/cortex/images/TIFF 16-BIT/t_NNN.tif (+ 2576px analysis JPEG for field_scale/gesture topology)
pipeline.output: data/measurements/<group>/T_NNN.json, one file per group, overwrite by work_id (deterministic)

groups.segmentation: A: elements (connected ink >= 0.5 cell length, orientation-split by structure tensor), splatter attached to parent elements (per-blob then per-cluster vote), independent residue (individual + populations with width/tone/interval constancy)
groups.boundary_profile: B: per-element per-cell edge segments; trait HARD | SOFT_FEATHERED | BROKEN_RAGGED | UNCERTAIN_BLOOM_FAMILY | UNCLASSIFIED from width/fill_ratio_p10/ring_depth/frag_count; mask_reconstruction_reliable flag
groups.pass_overlap: C: candidate cells (ink density >= 0.3 or >= 2 elements) with density, darkness, tone_std, band_area_fractions (9 bands), n_bands_occupying (bands >= 15% of cell), entropy, coherence, orientation peaks; not a verdict
groups.gesture_profile: D: per element skeleton longest path, width profile, endpoint fill/fragment evidence at radii 50/100/200/300 px, likely_failed (fill@200 <= 0.30, advisory), width_turn events
groups.field_scale: E: num_masses (blur sigma 0.08*short side, threshold band<=4, >=1% area), mass displacement label CENTRED|<compass>_SLIGHT|<compass>_MARKED (<0.05 / >0.15 of half-diagonal), element_groupings
groups.voids: held voids H1..: closing of structural ink (disk r=0.2*short side) AND paper with structural ink before/after along row or column within 2r; per void cells, area_fraction, held_axes, touches_edges, perimeter_by_cell{ink_edge_px, crisp_fraction (Sobel/8 >= 0.06)}, open_perimeter_fraction, marks_inside(+cells)
groups.orientation_field: structure tensor (sigma 0.01*short side) on ~1440px luma with specks painted out by grey closing (25px); axial angles 0-180 (0 horizontal, 90 vertical, CCW, y up); dominant family = histogram peak (36 bins); second family ('opposing' in the JSON) = peak >= 45 deg away and >= 0.35 of dominant; axial, so it cannot tell a movement from its reverse or a crossing from an opposition: the facts call them main and second families and the model decides opposition from the images; per-cell angle/strength; extent = share of 6 long-axis positions
groups.presence: deterministic/presence.py, v2.1: ink_coverage (share of sheet that is ink), darkest_share (share in the two darkest of nine bands), deepest_ink (5th-percentile ink luma), paper_tone (median non-ink luma), tonal_range, edge_mix from boundary_profile traits (crisp, soft_or_bloom, broken shares); grounds E1; run alone with process_computed.py --presence-only
groups.frame_contact: per edge N S W E: contact_fraction, runs (fractions along edge), margin_fraction; weight_centre (darkness below paper median tone) and densest_point (blur sigma 0.08) with cell and anchors within 0.05 (sheet centre, centre lines, edge midpoints)

shared.ink: Rec.709 luma quantised to 9 equal bands over 0-65535; ink = band <= 4 (darkest 5 of 9)
shared.grid: landscape 6 cols A-F x 3 rows; portrait 3 cols A-C x 6 rows; cell_at(x,y,w,h)
shared.sheet_view: deterministic/sheet.py: block-mean luma to ~1440px long side; structural_ink = ink minus components < 0.0005 of sheet

pipeline.name: lean ensembled classification + rating
pipeline.model_calls: 2 independent runs per painting, plus a third only as a tie-break on the axes they split (pipeline/tiebreak_step2.py); fresh Claude Code subagents on Opus 5.5 (no API key), one painting at a time, only with Peter's written go-ahead; measured about 110k subagent tokens and 2 min per full run, a tie-break about 76% of that
pipeline.prepare: pipeline/prepare_step2.py T_NNN: renders facts (step2/facts.py), fills prompts/step2_prompt_v2.md (step2/fill.py, refuses unfilled placeholders), writes data/step2_runs/T_NNN/{prompt.md, dispatch.md, manifest.json}; refuses if run*.json exist unless --force, which moves them to superseded-<timestamp>/
pipeline.run: each subagent reads prompt.md, views the 5 images in order, writes only the JSON object to runN.json; may read the schema, nothing else
resolve_algorithm: load runs listed in manifest; missing/unparseable file = invalid run

validate_run under the manifest's schema_version (v2 runs keep their 13-axis schema; v2.1 has 14): jsonschema Draft 2020-12 from step2/schema.py, unique part tags, P parts not VOID and V parts VOID, a P1, every cell on the sheet's grid for its orientation; work_id must equal the painting; invalid runs excluded, errors reported in runs_invalid

axis_errors per run: a value contradicting its own fields (B2 CLEAN with a marker, D1 above ACCEPTED with route NONE, A1 rung 3+ without HEAVY demand, D3 act counts, a rung resting on (C) with no counterfactual, a counterfactual target not among the parts, a survey entry with no cells, C4 master with fewer than four shift tests) drops only that run's vote on that axis (excluded_votes)
per axis per valid run: if value is rung 4, survey_contradictions(axis, record, measurements); any contradiction -> that run's value becomes rung 3 (recorded in downgrades)

majority via gemini_synthesis.agreement_from_values over final values: UNANIMOUS or MAJORITY (> half) resolves; SPLIT or DISPERSED -> value None; fewer than 2 valid runs -> None (SINGLE_RUN / NO_DATA); never averaged

master gate: resolved rung 4 stands only if all dispatched runs valid, every run's final value is that rung-4 value at confidence HIGH with non-empty master_survey, and no downgrade; else value = rung 3, gated=true, evidence strips master_survey and sets gated_from_rung_4

evidence = observation, rung_check, counterfactual, decision_note, master_survey, demand, markers, evidence_route, acts from one run, named in evidence_run: representative, not agreed wording; the first run whose value equals the resolved value, or after the gate the first run that chose rung 4 (never a dissenting lower reading); a standing rung 4 carries survey_verified (False = Step 1 could not check it, not cleared)
composition_mode and geometry voted the same way; parts_by_run and fact_conflicts (tagged by run) carried for Peter's review, never resolved in code

rating: weighted mean rung over axes with a rung, mapped through rating_weights.json anchors (piecewise linear, 0->1 and 4->10 fixed); NOT_PRESENT = inapplicable, left out; unresolved / NOT_ESTABLISHED = applicable but unsettled: left out of the point rating and reported as weight_coverage and rating_bounds (every unsettled axis at its lowest and at rung 4); provisional below 80% coverage or with a weight-2+ axis unsettled

survey_crosscheck.any_axis: a master_survey item with holds=false is a contradiction
survey_crosscheck.C1: find the first measured void (largest first) whose perimeter cells the survey covers at least half of; if none, no Step 1 check and survey_verified=False (model V1 need not be H1; large voids unmeasured); if found, every perimeter cell must be surveyed, each must have crisp_fraction >= 0.1 (a findable edge; soft limits allowed since v2.1), and open_perimeter_fraction must be <= 0.1
survey_crosscheck.A1: every pass_overlap candidate with n_bands_occupying >= 3 (marked 'tonally complex' in the facts; tonal variety, not a pass count) must appear in the survey cells
survey_crosscheck.C4: survey must contain items with edge N, S, E and W

pipeline.calibration_report: pipeline/calibration_report.py -> data/step2_results/calibration_report.md: per work Peter vs engine rating and unresolved axes; MAE; signed error overall and split at Peter 5; count more than a point off; Spearman engine vs Peter; D3 watch (rating with and without D3, D3 rung vs A1/A3/C1/C3); per axis unanimous/majority/unresolved counts, rung distribution 0-4, Spearman rung vs p_rating; rung-4 list (hand-check) and gated list

principles: Step 1 outranks the model: facts are authoritative in the prompt; conflicts go to fact_conflicts for Peter, never resolved by code or model
Step 1 is validated against Peter's eye (overlays), never against a model
every judgment that can be measured is measured first; the model judges only what measurement cannot reach
honesty through rarity, evenly spaced (Peter 2026-09-24): rung 0 structural failure (occasional), 1 competent (common), 2 strong (common), 3 excellent (occasional), 4 master (rare)
failure rungs are structural or dominant: a rung-0 fault must sit in a structural position, recur in two regions, or run through most of the sheet

whole-sheet axes (A1 A2 B1 B2 C2 C4 E1) are judged on the sheet as a whole; instance axes (A3 C1 C3 C5 D1 D2 D3) take the strongest instance only if it is in a principal part (P1-P3) or V1; replaced 'strongest instance decides' (2026-09-24), which let T_188's best fragments carry each axis

style-neutral: the body of work spans single gestures, all-over fields, centred masses, sparse marks, layered passes, soft and crisp voids; where a rung offers routes joined by 'or' they are equal (C2 centred-active, C3 single developed movement, C4 composed margins, C1 soft findable voids, A2 one held edge kind)
observation before value; rung_check states the next rung's condition and what fails it; 'conservative' is not a reason; no over-award warnings in the prompt
counterfactual C1-C3 on every rung claiming dependency: commit target+prediction, evaluate that prediction, ground at named cells
studio conditions are neutral: composite mega-brush seams, glued tufts, 3+ staged dilutions
prompt never mentions scoring or ratings; rating is code-only, weights readable/adjustable by Peter
consistency via ensembling (3 runs voted), not finer decomposition (the archived 14-step prompt showed 30-70% blind-read disagreement)
archive, never delete, retired work; never hand-edit 11-Painting-Archive (generated from cortex.db)
hard_rules_operational: no model/engine run without Peter's explicit written go-ahead each time
one painting at a time; never batch or parallelize model runs
Step 1 only under the 3 GB per-painting cap; never two capped heavy processes at once on the 8 GB VM
commit on main in ~/NEON (vault convention); attribution trailer per session instructions
no em dashes in Claude's prose to Peter

pipeline/prepare_step2.py.doc: Prepares one Step 2 dispatch packet per painting: the filled prompt, the five image paths in order, the schema, and the run file paths a fresh subagent writes to. Makes no model call. Refuses to touch a painting that already has run files unless --force, which moves them into superseded-<timestamp>/, so runs made against different prompts are never mixed. To re-run a painting that already has results under an earlier prompt version, use --tag (e.g. --tag v2_1): the new runs get their own folder and the earlier dispatch stays intact beside them.

defs.run_folder: Runs for a prompt/model variant live beside the main runs, never in them.

pipeline/process_computed.py.doc: STEP 1 (official terminology, Pete, 2026-09-17 -- see README.md's Terminology section: the deterministic scripts run on the images, and the JSON they produce). CLI driver for V22's five Step 1 groups -- Group A (segmentation.py), Group B (boundary_profile.py), Group C (pass_overlap.py), Group D (gesture_profile.py), and Group E (field_scale.py), plus (2026-09-23) held voids (void_detection.py), the orientation field (orientation_field.py) and frame contact (frame_contact.py) -- zero model calls, computed straight from each painting's TIFF master. Output lives under `data/measurements/<group>/`, one subfolder per themed group, one file per painting -- written individually, right after that painting finishes.

defs._read: A group this painting wrote earlier in the same run (staged) or, outside a run, the published one.
defs.process_presence: Presence only (grounds E1): reads this work's saved boundary_profile for the edge mix, so it can be backfilled without re-running the rest.

pipeline/process_interpretive.py.doc: STEP 3 (official terminology, Pete, 2026-09-17): the written prose, built from Step 1 and Step 2's settled data. Run AFTER `pipeline/resolve_step2.py` has resolved a painting's ensemble into `data/step2_results/T_NNN.json`. Decoupled from classification by design: this stage may not reach a different reading of any axis; it explains settled findings, so it only ever reads results that are already final.

pipeline/render_step1_overlays.py.doc: Draws the new Step 1 measurements over each painting's analysis image so Peter can check them by eye (spec: Step 1 is validated against Peter's read, never against the model). Held voids tinted cyan with their ink-facing limit green where crisp and red where not; per-cell movement direction as short lines (orange = dominant family, magenta = opposing, grey = neither); edge contact as yellow bars on the frame; weight centre as a white ring, densest point as a yellow ring.

pipeline/resolve_step2.py.doc: Resolves a painting's finished Step 2 runs: validate, cross-check, vote, gate, rate. Reads data/step2_runs/T_NNN/, writes data/step2_results/T_NNN.json (deterministic from the run files, so re-running overwrites). A missing or unparseable run file counts as an invalid run.

pipeline/results_notes.py.doc: Final engine ratings and their vault pages.

defs.finalize: One final rating per work. A tagged dispatch (e.g. a v2.1 re-run, T_188__v2_1) can be the final one; the ledger names which.

pipeline/step1_coverage.py.doc: Regenerates 16-VAE/v22/STEP1_COVERAGE.md: one row per painting with all eight Step 1 groups measured, linked to its page in the painting archive, plus the paintings that still have a TIFF but no complete Step 1 data. Generated from data/measurements and cortex.db (read-only); never hand-edit the output, re-run this instead.

pipeline/tiebreak_step2.py.doc: After runs 1 and 2: decide whether run 3 is needed. Two agreeing votes already decide an axis out of three, so run 3 is skipped when runs 1 and 2 agree on every axis; otherwise it is a tie-break that classifies only the split axes (a fresh, independent agent with the same prompt and images, but far less to think through and write). Rewrites the painting's manifest (runs = run1, run2; tiebreak = null or {run, axes}) and, for a split, writes schema_tiebreak.json and dispatch_tiebreak.md. An axis where either run contradicts itself (validate.axis_errors) has only one usable vote, so it goes to the tie-break too.

step2/axes.py.doc: The Step 2 axes, their five-rung ladders (index = rung) and the closed vocabularies of the Step 2 output. Single source of truth for the schema, the vote and the rating; the prompt's ladders must match it (checked in test_prompt_matches_registry).

step2/calibration.py.doc: Calibration set (spec, seed 20260923) and the report that answers the spec's three accuracy questions: consistency (repeat-run agreement per axis), gut agreement (engine rating vs Peter's p_rating), discriminative power (rank correlation overall and per axis). Also: signed error, split by lower- and higher-rated work (an engine that rates everything 6 can have a tolerable mean error and still be useless), and the D3 watch (Peter, 2026-09-24): whether Risk adds anything the axes it overlaps (A1, A3, C1, C3) do not already carry.

step2/crosscheck.py.doc: Checks a rung-4 master_survey against what Step 1 measured. Any contradiction caps that run's value at rung 3 (spec: "One contradiction caps the axis at rung 3"). Measured checks exist for the axes Step 1 reaches directly: C1 (when the survey covers a measured void: every limit cell of it surveyed, each with a findable edge, and no open stretch), A1 (every overlap cell the facts mark tonally complex surveyed), C4 (all four edges surveyed). Every axis also fails on a survey entry that itself records an exception.

defs._surveyed_void: The measured void the survey is about: the first (largest) whose limit cells the survey covers at least half of. None when the survey is about a void Step 1 did not measure (the model's V1 need not be H1, and voids wider than ~40% of the short side are not measured).
defs.survey_verified: Whether Step 1 measured what this rung-4 survey claims.

step2/facts.py.doc: Loads one painting's Step 1 measurements and renders them as the compact, cell-named lines the Step 2 prompt's known_facts block takes. Cells, words and shares only; no pixel coordinates reach the model.

step2/fill.py.doc: Fills the Step 2 template with rendered facts. Raises on a missing fact or a leftover placeholder rather than sending a half-filled prompt.

step2/images.py.doc: The five views Step 2 sends, in the prompt's order, from the live image master (/mnt/c/cortex/images -> C:\AA_CY_IMAGE_MASTER).

step2/rating.py.doc: Deterministic 1-10 rating from resolved axis rungs.

step2/schema.py.doc: Builds the JSON Schema every Step 2 run must satisfy, from the axis registry. `python -m step2.schema --write` regenerates one file per schema version (schema/step2_output_v2.schema.json, ..._v2.1.schema.json); a test keeps the files in sync. Old runs validate against their own version.

defs.build_tiebreak_schema: A third run that classifies only the axes runs 1 and 2 split on.

step2/validate.py.doc: Validation of one Step 2 run record. Returns readable error strings (empty = valid); never raises on bad model output.

defs.axis_errors: Per-axis self-contradictions of a record that passed validate_run.

step2/vote.py.doc: Resolves a painting's ensemble of Step 2 runs into one value per axis.
